Allen: a railroad town that doubled, then doubled again

Allen began as a stop on a railroad line built north through Collin County, and it was named in 1872 for Ebenezer Allen, a state politician and railroad promoter. It stayed small for a long time, with 1,940 residents in 1970. Then U.S. 75, DFW Airport and the spread of Dallas and Plano pushed growth north. Allen counted 8,314 people in 1980, 18,309 in 1990, 43,554 in 2000, 84,246 in 2010 and 104,627 in 2020, with the Census Bureau estimating about 113,000 by mid 2025.

Most of those homes went up in the 1990s and 2000s, and about 69 percent are lived in by their owners, according to the Census Bureau. That combination shapes AC calls in Allen: many owners are now deciding what to do with original or first replacement equipment, often in homes they plan to stay in.

Repair or replace: how to think it through in an Allen home

There is no single age when a system must go. These are the questions that usually decide it, and the company you are put through to can answer them for your equipment.

Signs a repair can make sense

  • The failed part is a capacitor, contactor, fan motor or drain problem.
  • The system has had few repairs before this one.
  • It cools evenly and keeps up when it is running.
  • It uses R-410A, which is still available for service.

Signs replacement deserves a look

  • The compressor has failed or the indoor coil is leaking.
  • It runs on R-22, which has not been produced or imported in the U.S. since 2020.
  • It has needed several repairs in a few summers.
  • Rooms upstairs never cool, even when the system works.

Whatever the answer, get it in writing: the diagnosis, the repair price and, if offered, the replacement price, all from the same visit.

Allen's 2024 codes and city registration

On July 28, 2026, Allen adopted the 2024 International Code Council building codes, including the 2024 International Mechanical Code, International Residential Code and International Energy Conservation Code. They took effect September 26, 2026, and the city reviews every permit application received on or after that date under the new codes. If you are replacing a system this fall or later, those are the rules the job is checked against.

Allen also requires contractors to register with the city every year through its Citizen Self-Service portal, separate from the state license. The city's list of residential work that needs no permit covers only small mechanical items, such as replacing a minor part that does not change the equipment's approval. A full system change is a bigger job, so ask the company to include the permit on its written quote. The city's Building and Permitting division answers permit questions directly.

Storms in Allen and what they mean for the outdoor unit

North Texas spring storms reach Allen too. An EF-1 tornado damaged about 50 homes in Allen in 2008, and an EF-0 touched down in west Allen in 2019. Most storm trouble for an air conditioner is less dramatic: hail that flattens the thin aluminum fins on the outdoor coil, limbs that land on the unit, and power that flickers on and off.

  1. Before the storm. Move patio furniture, grills and toys away from the condenser so wind cannot throw them into it.
  2. During an outage. Set the thermostat to Off until the power is back and steady, so the compressor does not restart during a string of flickers.
  3. After the storm. Walk around the outdoor unit. Look for dents, flattened fins, a damaged fan guard or debris inside the top grille.
  4. If anything looks wrong. Leave the system off and call. Photos of the damage help if you file a home insurance claim.

Power and gas in Allen

Allen is in Oncor's delivery area, so you choose a retail electric provider while Oncor maintains the lines and handles outages. If the lights are on but the AC is not, the problem is with the system, not the power company. Because Oncor delivers the power, Allen homes can look into Oncor's Home Energy Efficiency program, which pays incentives for some heating, cooling and insulation upgrades through approved service providers. Ask about it before you sign for new equipment.

For gas, check your bill to see which company serves your address. If you smell gas, get everyone out of the house without flipping switches, then phone 911 and your gas utility once you are in the yard or street. Keep both emergency numbers handy: 866-322-8667 for Atmos Energy and 844-330-0763 for CoServ. A beeping carbon monoxide detector calls for the same response, outside first and 911 next.

Common questions

My Allen house was built around 2005 and still has the original AC. Should I replace it?

Not on age alone. A capacitor, a fan motor or a clogged drain can be a reasonable repair on a 20 year old system. A failed compressor, a leaking indoor coil or repeated breakdowns make replacement easier to justify. Ask the company for a repair price and a replacement price on the same visit so you can compare them in writing.

Do HVAC companies have to register with the City of Allen?

Yes. Allen requires contractors to register with the city each year through its Citizen Self-Service portal, and it points HVAC contractors to the state license from TDLR as a separate requirement. Ask for that state license number and look it up online.

Did Allen change its building codes in 2026?

Yes. The city adopted the 2024 International Code Council codes, including the 2024 mechanical, residential and energy codes, effective September 26, 2026. Permit applications received on or after that date are reviewed under the new codes, so ask the company to confirm the permit for a replacement job.

What should I do with the AC when a storm is coming in Allen?

Nothing complicated. Clear loose patio items away from the outdoor unit, and if the power flickers or goes out, turning the thermostat off until service has settled keeps the compressor from cycling on and off. After a storm, look for hail damage, bent fins or limbs on the unit before turning it back on, and call a company if anything looks damaged.

Who is the electric company in Allen?

Oncor delivers power in Allen, and you pick the retail provider that sends the bill. Report outages to Oncor. Neither Oncor nor your provider repairs air conditioners.
